## LLM Recipe

### 1.2 Model Architecture &amp; Scaling Laws

#### [One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582>)

Elastic Latent Recurrence combines gated state updates, mixed loop counts within optimizer updates, and loop conditioning so one model can serve several inference depths while preserving competitive one-loop accuracy. Late mixed-depth training and cache reuse make this a practical recipe for trading additional computation for stronger answers within a fixed model footprint.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Recurrent Depth, Pretraining, Test-Time Compute

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–6 include matched-data 4B and 30B-A3B experiments: one-loop ten-task averages differ from non-recurrent baselines by -0.52/+1.04 points, and four loops improve over one loop by 7.25/4.75 points. Ablations isolate the training choices. The October 12 new-submission listing and official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC public announcement; this is inferred timing, distinct from the October 8 receipt date.

**Limitations:** Additional loops increase computation and latency. The 16% training overhead is a layer-execution estimate; Koi-4B has no matched non-recurrent control, and its AA scores are author-harness estimates. Last-loop caching changes attention semantics and retains separate GDP state. No released implementation or weights were verified.

#### [Multi-Stream Attention Residuals](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630>)

MSAR lets each layer retrieve earlier representations through several contextual views created by causal convolutions, then combines those views into one layer input. Its blockwise design stores a single stream of source summaries while improving pretraining results in the tested MoE models, offering an alternative to fixed residual addition and single-stream depth attention.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Residual Architecture, MoE, Scaling Laws

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 compare 18B/28B MoE models across 12 tasks; averages rise from AttnRes's 41.8/49.4 to 45.7/52.4. Four-scale fits estimate a 1.58x iso-loss compute advantage over standard residuals. The October 12 new listing and official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC public availability, distinct from the October 9 receipt date.

**Limitations:** The compute advantage is fitted, not measured wall-clock speedup; training-token budgets are omitted in the appendix tables. FLOPs estimates exclude recomputation and optimizer updates, and no multi-seed uncertainty is reported. Source-storage savings do not remove all intermediate memory traffic. The linked project failed to load twice, so code was not verified.

### 1.4 Mid-training &amp; Continual Learning

#### [Self-Preservation in Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12602>)

Task-Bank Self-Replay uses a frozen pre-update model to generate rehearsal data for selected task descriptions, then mixes that data into supervised adaptation. Experiments show that broader replay can protect capabilities outside the supplied task bank, while tracking previously correct answers reveals forgetting that aggregate accuracy can hide.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Continual Learning, Synthetic Replay, Capability Retention

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12602>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–3 study Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 4B with four replay tasks and four strictly held-out tasks. In the five-seed 4B MedQA comparison, incoming-aware selection achieves 95.69% held-out retention versus 92.94% for random selection. Public announcement is inferred as October 12 00:00 UTC from the dated new listing and official schedule; October 8 remains the submission date.

**Limitations:** Selection gains do not transfer to the smaller tested sizes. Most experiments cover one update; a two-stage pilot has mixed results. Fixed example counts do not match tokens or generation cost, and replay can reduce new-task learning. This does not demonstrate autonomous preservation of all capabilities. The linked repository is currently empty.

### 1.6 Preference Alignment &amp; Reward Modeling

#### [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707>)

This study trains a small linear reward head on frozen vision-language features by contrasting web captions with perturbed captions, avoiding human preference labels for head training while using labeled data to select the layer. It shows that strong reward-benchmark accuracy need not produce good candidate selection, and that retraining on verifier-labeled policy outputs can improve deployment-specific selection even as its VL-RewardBench score falls.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Reward Modeling, Multimodal, Negative Sampling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–3 test four Qwen3-VL sizes and GLM-4.1V-9B; Table 1 reports 72.4% VL-RewardBench accuracy for the 32B probe versus published GPT-4o's 65.8%. Section 3.4 tests one verifier-driven adaptation round. The actual October 12 new listing plus official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC announcement, not the October 8 submission timestamp.

**Limitations:** Layer selection uses labeled development data; benchmark rank is not general reward quality. CHAIR supplies both caption labels and evaluation, Best-of-N cells are single-seed, and matched-pair comparisons are not token-matched. The approximate 1/1000 training-compute claim excludes shared backbone forwards. Code release is promised but unverified.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.5 Agent Learning &amp; Skill Acquisition

#### [EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12789>)

EvoBelief keeps a frozen agent model while learning explicit rules about environment dynamics, testing those rules against observations and withdrawing their authority when counterexamples appear. The external belief system helps agents reuse verified knowledge across tasks and adapt to changing environments, with benchmark-specific code connecting supported rules to action predictions and plans.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:03:40Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** World Models, Test-Time Learning, Evidence Validation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12789>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–F describe the lifecycle, matched controls and diagnostics. On 134 ALFWorld tasks without actor transition memory, Table 1 reports 66.42% versus 42.54% success with Haiku 4.5 and 76.12% versus 44.78% with GPT-5.4 against Frozen WM; these are 23.88 and 31.34 percentage-point differences. October 12 NEW item 11 and the official Sunday announcement schedule support inferred public availability, preserving the October 8 submission date.

**Limitations:** Text environments and specialized adapters limit generality; the actor never receives rule text. Live experiments consume interaction budgets, and the full-system comparison does not isolate rule validation. The MiniGrid commitment-gate ablation is a null result. No author implementation was verified, and results were not reproduced.

#### [Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12601>)

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [VEPA: Verified Evolving Formal Policy for Lifelong LLM Agent Guardrails](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12813>)

VEPA uses a language model to propose symbolic guardrail updates, then checks rule structure and conflicts before granting supported rules permission to make deterministic decisions on parsed events. This separates policy learning from enforcement and improves the reported safety-versus-overrefusal tradeoff as feedback accumulates, while uncovered events require a separate fallback.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:03:40Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Guardrails, Formal Policies, Online Adaptation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12813>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–F specify search, evidence gating and five-seed prequential evaluation. On the same covered examples, final macro-F1 is 0.81 on ASSEBench-Safety and 0.76 on ATBench, exceeding the strongest baselines by 0.02 and 0.09; active coverage is approximately 80% and 88%. October 12 NEW item 12 plus the official Sunday schedule supports inferred public availability, preserving the October 8 submission date.

**Limitations:** Recorded trajectory streams do not test live behavioral feedback. Guarantees apply only after neural parsing and within a fixed schema, excluding fallback. The default posterior median gate reuses policy-selection data and is neither selection-adjusted nor time-uniform assurance. No author code was verified; results were not reproduced.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

#### [Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13325>)

GraphTok captures supported BPE-tokenizer operations in a reusable CUDA graph while preserving reference token IDs and routing small inputs to a CPU engine. Its new paper evaluates how tokenization affects long-context serving, separating gains in a real vLLM instance from the capacity of a shared Dynamo frontend.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:04:28Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Tokenization, CUDA Graphs, Serving Frontends

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13325>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Msiavashi/GraphTok>) · [Project](<https://msiavashi.github.io/GraphTok/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. On one H100 NVL, replacing stock vLLM tokenization lowers cold-cache mean TTFT only 2–4%, but gives 2.06–2.43× gains with 99% prefix reuse. A controlled Dynamo frontend sustains 518 versus gigatoken's 296 requests/s for 121K-token prompts under a 2-second P99 target.

**Limitations:** Dynamo uses simulated GPU workers: this is frontend capacity, not a measured 56-GPU serving deployment. Five tokenizer configurations, one GPU type and limited repeated trials; optimized CPU tokenization is close in the small vLLM experiment. Qwen normalization remains host-side.

**Update:** 2026-10-12: the newly announced paper supplies detailed serving experiments and controls beyond the implementation descriptions on GraphTok's October 9 first-release changelog and project page. The code's exact release time is unavailable, so no in-window first-release claim is made. Paper-update availability is inferred as October 12 00:00 UTC from https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/new and https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html; original v1 submission remains October 9. ### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778>)

ReplaySSM represents recurrent state as a checkpoint plus recent inputs, avoiding most full-state writes and making speculative rollback a buffer operation. The new paper extends this approach with separate precisions for output reads and recurrent updates, reducing the feedback of state-quantization error during long generations.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:04:28Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** SSM State, Speculative Decoding, Low Precision

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778>) · [Blog](<https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Johnny-Liou/ReplaySSM>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The new quantization study reports mean GPQA-Diamond losses of 13.05 percentage points for shared NVFP4+SR versus 2.36 for NVFP4 reads with FP16+SR recurrence across four hybrid models. Separately, FP32-state decoding at batch 256 improves whole-step latency by 1.20–1.47× on one H100 or B300 per model.

**Limitations:** Quantization accuracy uses emulation, standard decoding and full-precision prefill; residual errors remain. Performance gains shrink at batch 1. The public fork contains experimental paths beyond the upstream Mamba2 integration; benchmarks were not reproduced.

**Update:** 2026-10-12: the newly announced paper adds two-precision state algorithms and long-generation KL/accuracy experiments beyond the June 15 ReplaySSM blog (https://dao-lab.ai/blog/). The retained October 9 date is this arXiv paper's v1 submission date, not the method's first release. Paper-update availability is inferred as October 12 00:00 UTC from https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/new and https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html; the June method is not being presented as newly invented.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13474>)

CompileMask translates region-based attention visibility rules into batch-specific interval tables and tile metadata, moving repeated mask calculations out of the attention kernel. This supports configurable masking while retaining efficient execution, with measured gains in complete Qwen training steps as well as standalone operators.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:04:28Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Attention Kernels, Compiler, Training Throughput

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13474>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. For packed Qwen3-8B training with HSTU masks and KuaiRand length traces, throughput is 15.038 versus Flex-FA4's 11.325 kTok/s (1.33×), including preprocessing and full training steps. The same result is 3.83× Flex-Triton; these are different baselines.

**Limitations:** The paper specifies Blackwell GPUs but not an exact SKU. Its interval fast path requires bounded interval structure; unsupported predicates retain a callable fallback, and forward/backward specifications are supplied separately. No dedicated public code artifact was verified; no task-quality improvement is established.
